payload.rationale: I called perspective once with a focus on the owned-vs-rented intelligence thesis and the substrate/perspective positioning. The map and coverage were empty, and the doors reported 0 thematic areas, 0 dimensions, 0 documents and 0 unplaced items, with a single person (the submitter, Xena, as an actor). I expanded the Thematic door, which returned no areas, and the People door, which returned only that actor; the focus-scoped tail had no witness-depth match. I did not expand any Documents, Dimensions, or Unplaced doors because they reported zero entries. The document's two positioning quotes and its restated thesis have no existing position or narrative in this graph to bind to, so the passes should treat them as new material rather than revisions of anything surfaced here.

positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: Where does the owned part of intelligence sit when the substrate can be rented, and what does ownership of a perspective mean as distinct from ownership of the underlying model?
positions.why: The two parallel maxims (src-3, src-4) read in one direction: owned intelligence is opposed to rented intelligence, and the substrate is a commodity while the perspective is the asset kept. src-5 states that the segment restates the individually-owned-intelligence thesis, so it reads in the same direction as the maxims. The set is a single contrast framed as a thesis; it is stated, not argued, and no tension is held within it.
